title: Charge, energy and capacity

concepts.label: coulomb
concepts.definition: The unit of electric charge: 1 C is the charge of about 6.24 × 10¹⁸ electrons (one electron carries 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).

concepts.label: ampere
concepts.definition: The unit of current: 1 A is one coulomb passing a point per second, so charge = current × time.

concepts.label: Faraday constant
concepts.definition: F = 96 485 C, the charge of one mole of electrons; charge = n × moles of metal × F converts between amount of substance and coulombs.

concepts.label: volt = joule per coulomb
concepts.definition: A voltage of 1 V gives 1 joule of energy to each coulomb pushed through the circuit, so energy (J) = charge (C) × voltage (V).

concepts.label: Gibbs energy ΔG = −nFE
concepts.definition: ΔG is the energy a reaction can hand over as work; for a cell reaction ΔG° = −nFE°cell (J per mole of reaction), negative when E° is positive, i.e. when the reaction is spontaneous.

concepts.label: ampere-hour (capacity)
concepts.definition: Capacity is the total charge a cell can deliver, counted in ampere-hours: 1 Ah = 3600 C, 1 mAh = 3.6 C; runtime = capacity ÷ current.

concepts.label: watt (power)
concepts.definition: Power is the rate of delivering energy: 1 W = 1 J/s, and power (W) = voltage (V) × current (A).

concepts.label: watt-hour (energy)
concepts.definition: The everyday unit of stored energy: 1 Wh = 3600 J, and energy (Wh) = capacity (Ah) × voltage (V).

concepts.label: specific capacity (mAh/g)
concepts.definition: Theoretical charge per gram of an electrode material: n × F / (3.6 × M) mAh/g for n electrons per formula unit of molar mass M (Zn 820, Li 3862, Al 2980, Pb 259).

concepts.label: specific energy (Wh/kg)
concepts.definition: Energy per unit mass: specific capacity (mAh/g) × cell voltage (V) = Wh/kg, per kilogram of whatever is counted (anode only, all reactants, or the whole cell).

namedOnly: joule (recalled as the physics unit of energy, not a course concept)
practical vs theoretical energy density (pointer to Real batteries)
summary: Running example: a 6.54 g (0.100 mol) zinc strip consumed in the Daniell cell at 1.10 V, followed through every unit: 0.200 mol e⁻ → 19 297 C → 5.36 Ah → 21.2 kJ = 5.9 Wh, ΔG° = −212 kJ/mol, 820 mAh/g, and 902 → 457 → 262 Wh/kg as the copper ions and sulfate are counted. Capstone: a 'design a gram' calculator (anode Li/Na/Mg/Al/Zn/Fe/Pb × cathode Cu²⁺/Ag⁺/Cl₂/O₂) showing the chain grams → mol e⁻ → C → mAh → V → Wh → Wh/kg with and without cathode mass. Hooks for later lessons: Chem.capacity(n, M) values, 'mAh/g × V = Wh/kg', 'per kilogram of what?', ΔG° = −nFE° as the ceiling on electrical work, and energy drawn as a charge × voltage rectangle.
